personality_one_liner: A highly evolved, cinematic scientific instrument that translates the invisible universe into an elegant, sensory-rich experience.

spacing.rule: Generous Apple-style padding (lg/xl). Content modules are separated by obvious whitespace or structural glass cards. Safe areas must be perfectly respected for the full-bleed AR/3D screens.

do's: Use heavily blurred glass (expo-blur) for floating UI controls over AR/Camera and 3D views.
Use glassmorphism for bottom sheets containing astronomical facts.
Use subtle glass for the module cards on the Home screen layered over the animated space background.
dont's: Do not use glass for text containers if contrast drops below 4.5:1. Always pair glass with a >70% opacity dark tint underlay.
Do not over-layer glass on top of glass; keep it to one elevated layer.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Minimalist launchpad acting as the index to the universe.

states.loading: Subtle pulsing brandPrimary (Gold) abstract logo on pure black.
states.error: Minimal text 'Connection lost to the cosmos' with a retry button.

screens.layout: Full-bleed abstract animated background. Top: minimal 'Overview' wordmark. Center: The philosophical quote fading in and out slowly. Bottom 2/3: A beautifully spaced grid (or list) of frosted glass cards for the 8 modules. No tab bar. Stack navigation pushes to modules.

screens.name: Qui_e_Ora
screens.purpose: Real-time narrative data dashboard of Earth and Space.
screens.layout: Apple Weather style. Large scrolling list of glass cards. The hero card is the narrative sentence ('Earth is currently moving at...'). Below it, a 2-column grid of square cards for metrics (Moon phase, Solar time, Magnetism) featuring large Mono typography.

screens.name: Cielo_AR
screens.purpose: Camera overlay showing the visible and invisible sky.

states.error: Camera access required for AR view.

screens.layout: Full-screen camera view with an overlay of stars/planets. Floating glass controls (back button, filters) avoid the safe areas. Tapping an object slides up a glass bottom sheet with facts, distance, and 3D images.

screens.name: Univers_3D
screens.purpose: 3D navigable solar system and nearby stars.
screens.layout: Immersive dark canvas. Floating minimalistic zoom/pan controls. A timeline scrubber at the bottom (floating glass pill) to move forward/backward in time.

screens.name: Realta_Invisibile
screens.layout: Aesthetic instrument panel. Large centralized abstract visualizations (e.g., a fluid compass or magnetic wave graph) that respond live to device movement. Mono fonts for precise numerical readouts.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly adhere to the 'Black, Gold, Blue' palette. Use the specified hex codes to maintain the cinematic, premium scientific instrument feel.

Typography: Use 'Geist' for all standard UI text. CRITICAL: For all scientific data numbers, coordinates, speeds, and live metrics (especially in 'Qui e Ora' and 'Realtà Invisibile'), you MUST use a Monospace font like 'Geist Mono' or 'Space Mono' to give it a precise, hardware-instrument aesthetic.

All navigation should use Stack layout. Home is the central hub. AR, 3D, and Camera screens must be completely full-bleed, extending under the notch/dynamic island and home indicator, with floating glass controls respecting safe areas.
Do NOT use purely flat design for the modules. Utilize 'expo-blur' heavily with a dark underlay (#1A1D24 at 75% opacity) to create Apple-style frosted glass cards over the deep space backgrounds.
Incorporate smooth, soft, and deliberate animations (Reanimated). State changes should feel like a high-end tool calibrating, not a playful app bouncing. Cap spring bounciness to 0.
For the AR and 3D views, ensure the UI chrome is kept to an absolute minimum, relying on gestures and floating glass pills.
No sci-fi tropes (no neon green grids, no cyber-punk fonts). The aesthetic is modern luxury space-tech (think Apple Watch Ultra or a minimalist Leica camera interface).
